name: Central bank stress
value: Fed weighs 50bp on 9 Dec; yen near ¥160/$
summary: Markets weigh a large Fed rise on 8–9 Dec despite administration calls for restraint; yen held just below ¥160/$
state: Markets see a 50bp Federal Reserve rise at the 8–9 Dec meeting as possible after a third above-forecast inflation print, while Treasury Secretary Bessent has argued against large rises and President Trump favours cuts (The Edge Malaysia, 17 Nov). The yen tested ¥160 per dollar for the third time this year in mid-November, drawing warnings from Finance Minister Katayama, after Japan spent ¥27.1tn on intervention in 2026 (FXStreet, 13 Nov); it stayed below ¥160 in the week to 20 Nov (MUFG). No emergency move, coordinated intervention or attempt to remove a central-bank head was found as of 28 Nov.
for_you: Borrowers on variable rates and those refinancing in the US are most exposed to further Fed rises. Japanese importers and travellers to Japan are affected by yen swings; intervention, when it comes, tends to move the currency sharply in a short time.
rubric_hit: Watch: open political pressure on the Fed and G7 FX intervention risk (yen ~¥160/$); no emergency moves or coordinated action

sources.title: The Edge Malaysia — Markets weigh rare 50bp Fed hike as Bessent urges restraint
FXStreet — The Japanese yen's 160 line just got its third test of the year

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
